`MessagingAttributesGetter.getErrorType()` now supplies the final `error.type`. Returning `null` omits the attribute, even with an exception; the default still returns the exception class name.

Overrides that relied on extractor fallback can return the exception class directly:

```java
return customType != null
    ? customType
    : error == null ? null : error.getClass().getName();
```

Camel and RocketMQ retain their existing classification precedence. This is a breaking 3.0 contract change; extractors no longer replace a getter's `null` result.
metadata.title: Make messaging getters own final error.type classification
